title: Microsoft Viva: Organizational Data in Microsoft 365 for GCC-Moderate tenants
summary: Hold because the briefing incorrectly says uploading blank values deletes existing data. Microsoft's import instructions say blank values preserve existing values and require explicit deletion values instead. The roadmap facts and control routes are supported, with minor corrections to control details and qualifications.

claims.claim: Giving organizational data precedence changes profile-card values where sources provide different values.
claims.quote: If you assign data precedence to organizational data, when an experience like Profile cards in Microsoft 365 queries the Microsoft 365 User Profile to get the jobTitle property for that end user, "Senior Software Engineer" is returned instead of "Software Engineer."

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends regular refreshed uploads, for example weekly, to prevent stale profile data.
claims.quote: we recommend that you upload refreshed organizational data regularly (for example, weekly). This regular upload prevents the data in the user profile from becoming stale

claims.claim: An upload with blank values overwrites and effectively immediately deletes the user's existing data when processed.
claims.quote: If you include an attribute but leave the value blank or empty, the previously uploaded value will be used and the existing value won't be updated. New uploads merge with previous data and don't overwrite that data.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'Microsoft's import instructions say blank or empty values preserve previously uploaded values; deleting values requires explicit deletion values rather than ordinary blank cells.' The cited data-usage page describes deletion using nulled values and links to these import instructions; it does not justify equating plain blank cells with deletion.
